analysis.evidence: גַם הִוא יָלְדָה (‘she too bore’) resumes Zillah with a feminine singular pronoun and identifies her as the mother of Tubal-cain.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a feminine singular personal name.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the second of Lamech’s two wives.

analysis.evidence: In וְצִלָּה גַם הִוא יָלְדָה, גַם modifies הִוא, which refers back to Zillah. The phrase means “she too bore,” adding Zillah alongside Adah.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew adverb with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: הִוא refers back to צִלָּה. In גַם הִוא יָלְדָה, ‘she too bore,’ the pronoun agrees with the feminine singular verb יָלְדָה, and גַם supplies ‘too.’
analysis.morphology: Third-person feminine singular independent pronoun, written הִוא and read הִיא, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: יָלְדָה agrees with the feminine singular subject צִלָּה (Zillah), reinforced by גַם הִוא (‘she too’). אֶת marks תּוּבַל קַיִן (Tubal-cain) as the child she bore.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person feminine singular

analysis.evidence: In יָלְדָה אֶת תּוּבַל קַיִן, the proper name תּוּבַל קַיִן identifies the child Zillah bore. אֶת marks that name as the definite direct object of יָלְדָה.
analysis.morphology: Unsuffixed direct-object particle in the short form אֶת.

draft.change: Link the marked occurrence to the bearer already recorded in the Tubal-cain article.
draft.definition: Tubal-cain is the personal name of Zillah’s son, whom Genesis associates with work in bronze and iron.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:22 gives the full name in the birth notice and repeats it when naming his sister Naamah.

analysis.evidence: Zillah bears אֶת תּוּבַל קַיִן. The verse repeats both components in וַאֲחוֹת תּוּבַל קַיִן נַעֲמָה, identifying Naamah as Tubal-cain’s sister. This establishes the full name. Its derivation is uncertain.
analysis.morphology: תּוּבַל is the first component of a masculine singular personal name. It has no prefix or suffix. The preceding אֶת marks the full name as the direct object of יָלְדָה.
analysis.sense: Personal name of Zillah’s son, the brother of Naamah.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Tubal-cain with his verified bearer. Remove the earlier draft’s proposed link to qayin. That article names Eve’s son Cain, and the verse supplies no etymological root for Tubal-cain.
draft.definition: Tubal-cain, the son of Zillah and brother of Naamah, associated with work in bronze and iron.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:22 gives the same two-part name at the child’s birth and when identifying his sister. The local person record identifies him as Tubal-cain@Gen.4.22.

analysis.evidence: Zillah bears the child named in יָלְדָה אֶת תּוּבַל קַיִן. The verse repeats the full name in וַאֲחוֹת תּוּבַל קַיִן נַעֲמָה, identifying Naamah as his sister and confirming that the marked קַיִן belongs to the child’s name.
analysis.morphology: קַיִן is the second component of a masculine singular personal name and has no prefix or suffix. The object marker אֶת introduces the full name as the direct object of יָלְדָה.
analysis.sense: Tubal-cain, Zillah’s son and Naamah’s brother.

analysis.evidence: כָּל modifies the singular participle חֹרֵשׁ, “worker,” yielding “every worker of bronze and iron.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state.

analysis.evidence: חֹרֵשׁ is the active participle. The metals name what the worker works, so כָּל חֹרֵשׁ נְחֹשֶׁת וּבַרְזֶל means ‘every worker of copper and iron.’ לֹטֵשׁ literally means ‘one who sharpens.’ With the workers as its object, I read it figuratively of honing their skill and translate the whole phrase ‘one who honed the skill of every worker of copper and iron.’ The word ‘skill’ makes the metaphor explicit in English.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular construct, used substantivally.

analysis.evidence: The phrase חֹרֵשׁ נְחֹשֶׁת וּבַרְזֶל pairs נְחֹשֶׁת with iron as materials a smith works. The verse leaves open whether the metal is copper or bronze.

draft.change: Add Genesis 4:22 as evidence for the existing material sense of בַּרְזֶל.
draft.definition: Iron as a metal worked by a craftworker.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:22 names iron alongside copper in its description of Tubal-cain’s craft.

analysis.evidence: In חֹרֵשׁ נְחֹשֶׁת וּבַרְזֶל, the conjunction pairs iron with copper as the two metals a craftworker works.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: In וַאֲחוֹת תּוּבַל קַיִן נַעֲמָה, the construct noun takes תּוּבַל קַיִן as its complement, and the clause identifies Naamah as Tubal-cain’s sister.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular construct noun.

analysis.evidence: The birth notice names Zillah’s son תּוּבַל קַיִן. At the marked occurrence, וַאֲחוֹת תּוּבַל קַיִן נַעֲמָה repeats his full name and identifies Naamah as his sister. The verse gives no derivation for the name.
analysis.morphology: תּוּבַל is the first element of a masculine singular personal name and has no prefix or suffix. The full name follows אֲחוֹת, the construct form meaning “sister of.”
analysis.sense: Tubal-cain, son of Zillah and brother of Naamah

draft.change: Assign this occurrence to the existing Tubal-cain article and clear the published analysis’s unsupported root קינ. The current article already records the bearer and the verse evidence.

analysis.evidence: יָלְדָה אֶת תּוּבַל קַיִן names the son Zillah bore. At the marked occurrence, וַאֲחוֹת תּוּבַל קַיִן נַעֲמָה repeats his full name and identifies Naamah as his sister. The verse gives no derivation for the name.
analysis.morphology: קַיִן is the second element of a masculine singular Hebrew personal name. It has no prefix or suffix. The full name follows אֲחוֹת, the construct form meaning “sister of.”
analysis.sense: The personal name of Zillah’s son, identified here as Naamah’s brother.

analysis.evidence: The verbless clause וַאֲחוֹת תּוּבַל קַיִן נַעֲמָה means “and Tubal-cain’s sister was Naamah.” The kinship term אֲחוֹת identifies her as his sister.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
